_comment: Loading-screen filler for the blocking overlay (boot, refresh, purge, file queue...). One random line from the whole pool, flattened across every category; the category only picks the small caption shown above it (see _labels). 'idle' is separate: the lines the phone remote rotates through when nothing is playing. All lines here are original or plain common knowledge. A personal pack can replace this file wholesale.
tips: The Source dropdown starts on "Digital only" every time. If something you own on disc seems missing, switch it.
Purge never deletes anything: watched episodes are moved to a Pending Deletion folder for you to review.
Recently Watched remembers the last 12 things you checked off, in order.
A show set to "Delete after watching" keeps being tracked, so new episodes still show up.
Clicking a coloured status dot in the legend filters the grid by it. Click again to clear.
Marking a title "not interested" only affects that person's view, never anyone else's.
The nightly refresh picks up new files on its own. The Refresh button just does it now.
Wrong match? The Admin panel can fix a poster or re-point a title to the right TMDB entry.
Nothing is ever renamed or moved without a plan you can read first.
Drop a .mediaboxignore file in a folder and the scanner will leave it alone.
On a phone, the remote page shows just the transport controls, with no library to scroll past.
Season rows collapse for long shows. A season's own checkbox marks the whole thing at once.
weird_facts: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
Honey found in ancient tombs was still edible. It barely spoils.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Wombat droppings are cube-shaped, which keeps them from rolling away.
Bananas are berries. Strawberries are not.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
Sea otters sometimes hold paws while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
The Eiffel Tower grows a few centimetres taller on hot days.
The shortest recorded war, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896, lasted under an hour.
Scotland's national animal is the unicorn.
Crows can recognise individual human faces and remember them for years.
Lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
media_trivia: Silent films were rarely silent. Theatres hired live musicians, sometimes a whole orchestra.
The Lumiere brothers held one of the first paid public film screenings in Paris in 1895.
Film settled on 24 frames per second when sound arrived, partly so the audio would sound right.
A MacGuffin is an object that drives the plot while mattering very little in itself.
For decades, TV screens were 4:3. Widescreen 16:9 only became standard in the 2000s.
The Wilhelm scream is a stock sound effect that has turned up in hundreds of films.
The first feature-length cel-animated film arrived in 1937.
A cold open is the scene that plays before the title sequence. Many series use one.
Foley artists recreate everyday sounds, like footsteps and door creaks, in a studio, in sync with the picture.
A season finale that ends mid-story, on purpose, is called a cliffhanger.
dad_jokes: I only know 25 letters of the alphabet. I don't know y.
Why don't scientists trust atoms? They make up everything.
I used to hate facial hair, but then it grew on me.
What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta.
I'm reading a book about anti-gravity. It's impossible to put down.
Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field.
I would tell you a construction joke, but I'm still working on it.
What did the ocean say to the shore? Nothing, it just waved.

fortune: A quiet evening and a good episode: the best kind of plan.
The thing you almost skipped will be your favourite.
Someone will soon recommend a show you will watch in one weekend.
Good things come to those who wait for the buffering to finish.
You will find the remote exactly where you left it.
A pause today saves a rewind tomorrow.
The sequel is better than you were told.
Rest is also a plot point.
